To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the MND ANAs in patients without PSC/AMA are associated with binding to an immunologically distinct 70 kDa antigen, and not with a previously described 53 kDa protein that is found in those with PSC/AMA.
the 70 kDa antigen is immunologically distinct and is associated with autoimmune disorders other than PBC.
MND ANA is associated with binding of a 70 kD nuclear protein in patients without PSC/AMA and that this protein is immunologically distinct to the MND ANAs found with PSC/AMA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the nuclear antigen in sera from patients without PBC that produced a MND immunofluorescent pattern.
the identification of a novel nuclear protein in patients with MND ANA without PBC/ AMA.
the identification of a 70 kda protein associated with MND ANA and not found in PBC/AMA patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MND pattern in patients without PRC/AMA is associated not with a 100 kDa protein, but rather a 70 kD protein.
the MND pattern is associated with the 70 kDa antigen and that the 53 kDa (apparent molecular weight 100 kDa on SDS-PAGE) is associated with MND and AMA in PBC.
the MND ANAs in PBC/AMA patients are due to a different antigenic determinant than those without PBC/ANA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MND ANA without PBC/AM is associated with binding of a 70 kD antigen.
the MND ANAs are not all the same.
MND ANA is not specific for PBC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiple nuclear dot antinucle-ar antibody in patients without PRC/AMA is not associated with the 53 kDa/100 kDa antigen found in those with primary biliary disease.
MND is a pattern of ANA that is not unique to primary biliary cirrhotis.
MND-ANA is associated with binding a 70 kDA nuclear protein.
